meta.summary: Hides the bookmark banner and share card; toggles for shelves, schedule, comments, recommendations; blur episode spoilers and posters
meta.notes:
# Verified 2026-11-17

Opened https://www.miruro.to/ in headless WebKit logged out, desktop 1440x900 and an iPhone UA at 390px, and ran every rule's selector against four real pages: home, a watch page with a long episode list (grid layout, ONE PIECE), a watch page with a short list (image-and-title rows, 7 episodes) and an info page. The site is a React SPA with CSS-module class names whose trailing hash changes per build, so each selector matches the stable name prefix (`[class*="_scheduleSlot_"]`) and anchors on a role, tag, href or aria-label where it can. `miruro.tv` serves the same app (same title and shell), so it is matched too; `miruro.com` is a separate landing page and is not.

# Live match counts

- Home, both viewports: banner 1, Love the Site 1, carousel 1 (8 slides), genre strip 1, Your Watchlist shelf 1 (appears once you have watched something on this browser), Top Airing, Upcoming, schedule and Just Finished/Top Movies 1 each, SUB/DUB counters 27.
- Watch pages: 7 image rows with thumbnail, title and description in the short-list layout; the long-list layout shows only numbers, so thumbnails, titles and descriptions only exist there for short shows. Related and Recommendations aside 1, comments panel 1 (desktop), viewer count 1, tracker links 2.
- Info page: Recommendations row 1, trailer iframe 1, comments 1, 18 cover and recommendation pictures.
- Random Anime button: desktop top bar only.

# Choices worth knowing

- Top Airing and Upcoming are the first and second children of the home side column. They carry only an uppercase header text, which CSS cannot match, so those two rules follow that order. The whole-column option is the safe fallback if the order changes.
- The site has its own Hide episode spoilers toggle on the watch page; the thumbnail, title and description options here are always-on versions of it.
- English `aria-label` values (Episode availability, Edit List, Add to List, Random Anime, Recommendations) are used; they will not match a translated interface.

# Not verified

- Logged-in views (own list, notifications, profile menu contents), the settings and history pages, and the schedule, trending and search pages.
- The player itself: it is a separate frame (`strmcx-embed`), its ads, overlays, and the Auto next and Auto skip switches in its toolbar are player state that CSS cannot change. No ad slots or pop-ups were present in any page checked.
- The comments panel on a phone-width watch page loaded lazily and was not present at capture; its rule is checked on desktop only.
- The fixtures are trimmed, text-stripped captures of the real DOM, not full pages.
